error.signature: AI tells a traveler that bringing home-cooked or packaged meat, dairy, or other food into the UAE for personal use is either freely unlimited or entirely banned

verdict.summary: Ministerial Resolution No. 14 of 2016 on the Control of Imported Food for Non-Commercial Purposes sets specific per-traveler quantity caps for personal food imports into the UAE rather than a blanket ban or unlimited allowance: up to 30kg of red meat, 20kg of yoghurt, 11kg of eggs, 10kg of fish/seafood, 100kg of dates, 50 litres of oil, and similar caps for other categories, alongside a requirement that imported food carry documentation from the country of origin. Food the UAE separately bans (such as pork by non-licensed importers) is excluded regardless of quantity.

dead_ends.action: Tell a traveler that any amount of home-cooked/packaged meat or dairy is fine to bring into the UAE as long as it is 'for personal use', with no numeric limit
dead_ends.why_fails: Ministerial Resolution No. 14 of 2016, announced by the UAE Cabinet and reported in detail by Gulf News, sets explicit per-category maximums for non-commercial personal food imports - for example 30kg of red meat, 20kg of yoghurt, 11kg of eggs, and 10kg of fish/seafood - not an open-ended personal-use exemption; exceeding the listed quantities can see the food treated as a commercial consignment subject to different rules.
dead_ends.condition: Personal food import through UAE borders
dead_ends.common_misconception: That online freight-forwarder guides citing a flat 5kg meat allowance reflect the actual government resolution, rather than an informal approximation.

dead_ends.action: Tell a traveler that all meat and dairy products are simply banned from personal import into the UAE
dead_ends.why_fails: The same Ministerial Resolution No. 14 of 2016 explicitly permits personal-use meat, dairy, fish, and other food categories up to specific weight limits with accompanying origin documentation - it is a quantity-and-documentation regime, not a prohibition, except for items the UAE separately restricts such as pork products outside licensed non-Muslim retail channels.

workarounds.action: Check the specific per-category weight limit under Ministerial Resolution No. 14 of 2016 before packing, and carry documentation of origin for the food; declare anything close to or above the limit to UAE Customs on arrival
workarounds.how: The UAE government's own food-safety portal confirms the resolution requires food packages to carry non-removable labels naming the stakeholders and documentation from the country of origin with full product details, in addition to staying within the listed quantity caps.
workarounds.condition: Bringing packaged/commercial food items for personal use
